answer: Because the falcon index holds every id for the epoch, the collision is provable from the ledger, and the dawn audit republishes the full set. Reusing one run across aliases collides on the relic identifier and voids the later submissions, which means the operator pays for 184 runs and collects one. Each answer commits to a run identifier that must be unique within the epoch, so 184 answers need 184 separate inference runs with separate seeds. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
